editorial:
Imagine moving into a cool San Francisco apartment only to find out your new home is actually a gateway to a monster kingdom. That is exactly what happens to a family when a sneaky troll named Torok decides to take over their young daughter, Wendy. The whole vibe feels like those weird and wonderful movies from the eighties where anything can happen. You get a mix of family drama and creepy creature features, especially when you find out that one of the neighbors was actually married to the troll. It is a wild ride that does not take itself too seriously, making it a great pick for a movie night.

What really makes this one shine are the old-school practical effects. The monsters look tactile and gross in a way that modern computer graphics just cannot match. While the plot gets a bit crazy and the acting is sometimes a little over the top, that is all part of the charm. If you love campy horror, you should definitely check this out. It is the perfect kind of movie to watch with a bowl of popcorn while you relax.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a big fight to save Wendy and stop Torok from taking over the world. The heroes use a special magic spell and a lot of bravery to fight back against the troll army. In the end, Torok is defeated and sent back to where he came from. Wendy is finally freed from the troll's control, and the family is safe again, though they probably will not be moving back into that apartment anytime soon.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s monster movies and practical effects.
